The quiet hum of an early morning is my favorite kind of silence. It’s not the absence of sound but the presence of possibility—the way the first light filters through the curtains, painting the room in soft gold. I love how the world feels still before it wakes up, like a held breath before the exhale.

Sometimes, I wonder about the people who rush past me on the street, their faces locked in the glow of their phones. Do they ever pause to notice the way rain bends light or how a stranger’s smile can linger like a half-remembered dream? I think about the stories hidden behind their hurried steps—the barista who writes poetry in the margins of receipts, the old man feeding pigeons in the park, the teenager scribbling lyrics in a notebook during lunch. We’re all just fragments of someone else’s story, aren’t we?

And then there’s the ocean. The way it never stays the same—sometimes a mirror, sometimes a storm, always vast and unapologetic. It reminds me that change isn’t something to fear but something to embrace. Even the tides have to retreat to come back stronger.

I don’t know what tomorrow will bring, but I know this: I want to be present for it. To notice the small things—the warmth of a cup of tea, the sound of rain on a tin roof, the way a laugh can brighten even the dullest day. Life isn’t about grand gestures; it’s about the quiet moments that stitch together the tapestry of a life well-lived.

So here’s to the ordinary. Here’s to the unnoticed. Here’s to the beauty in the everyday.
